tags.name: bundle_items
tags.description: Bundle Items are components that make up a bundle, defining the quantity and relationship of items within product bundles.

tags.name: consumer_returns
tags.description: A ConsumerReturn represents goods coming back from an end consumer. It is a special form of Shipnotice, and is processed in much the same way.

tags.name: customers
tags.description: Customers are Whiplash clients, not the End Consumer. Most Whiplash resources are owned by a Customer (or belong to resources that are).

tags.name: documents
tags.description: Documents are imported files and exported reports. We store a record in your account of every file you import, as well as every report you've run, so they're easy to search and access.

tags.name: items
tags.description:
Items are probably the most fundamental entity in the Whiplash system. An item is simply a 'shippable unit'. So, it's not a Whiplash T-Shirt; it's a Small Whiplash T-Shirt, for instance.
Most commerce platforms model Products. Typically, however, a Product (e.g. a T-Shirt) has variations (named variously, Variants, ProductOptions, OptionSets, etc). An Item maps to the Variant/Option, not the Product.

tags.name: order_items
tags.description: An OrderItem represents an Item with a quantity in an Order.

tags.name: orders
tags.description:
Orders are end consumer requests for Items. An Order is comprised of OrderItems.
Orders represent outgoing stock.

tags.name: originators
tags.description:
Originators are e-commerce, API, or ERP representations of an Item, Order, OrderItem, ConsumerReturn, Shipnotice, or ShipnoticeItem. They contain your system's ID and, optionally, details.
You can use your own ID to retrieve, update, and destroy resources directly.

tags.name: shipnotice_items
tags.description: Similar to an OrderItem, ShipnoticeItem represents an Item with a quantity in a Shipnotice. quantity refers to the quantity expected to arrive, and the quantity actually received is quantity_good.

tags.name: shipnotices
tags.description:
A Shipnotice is the opposite of an order, and are notifications by the client of inventory that is expected to arrive at a warehouse.
Shipnotices represent incoming stock.

tags.name: simulate
tags.description: (Sandbox Only) Simulate Order and Ship Notice processing, since these are staff-only operations.

tags.name: templates
tags.description: Templates allow you to customize packing slips, email confirmations, order inserts, etc.
